You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 6b82f61dba6a569a5a2c240d08d3a600fd35b94d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ting-Wei Lan <lantw@src.gnome.org>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2015 18:37:20 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] build: Fix non-wayland build

This fixes error introduced in 09120132ef87061d527b5324a14ab5950db3dc0a.

https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=750552
---
 src/core/window.c | 4 ++++
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+)

diff --git a/src/core/window.c b/src/core/window.c
index 4443a2402..aec61db27 100644
--- a/src/core/window.c
+++ b/src/core/window.c
@@ -724,9 +724,11 @@ meta_window_should_attach_to_parent (MetaWindow *window)
 static gboolean
 client_window_should_be_mapped (MetaWindow *window)
 {
+#ifdef HAVE_WAYLAND
   if (window->client_type == META_WINDOW_CLIENT_TYPE_WAYLAND &&
       !window->surface->buffer)
     return FALSE;
+#endif
 
   return !window->shaded;
 }
@@ -1538,9 +1540,11 @@ meta_window_showing_on_its_workspace (MetaWindow *window)
 gboolean
 meta_window_should_be_showing (MetaWindow  *window)
 {
+#ifdef HAVE_WAYLAND
   if (window->client_type == META_WINDOW_CLIENT_TYPE_WAYLAND &&
       !window->surface->buffer)
     return FALSE;
+#endif
 
   /* Windows should be showing if they're located on the
    * active workspace and they're showing on their own workspace. */
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the code not being properly guarded with preprocessor directives to handle non-Wayland builds. The existing checks for Wayland-specific conditions were causing compilation errors in environments where Wayland support was not enabled, resulting in the inability to build the software. The patch added preprocessor conditions (`#ifdef HAVE_WAYLAND`) to ensure that the Wayland-specific code is only compiled when appropriate, thereby fixing the build issue for non-Wayland environments.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the code not being properly guarded with preprocessor directives to handle non-Wayland builds. The existing checks for Wayland-specific conditions were causing compilation errors in environments where Wayland support was not enabled, resulting in the inability to build the software. The patch added preprocessor conditions (`#ifdef HAVE_WAYLAND`) to ensure that the Wayland-specific code is only compiled when appropriate, thereby fixing the build issue for non-Wayland environments.
